entry.title: Light and colours
entry.coverage: One text per region, on the nature of light, its speed, and colours. read_from records what was read: 'image' where the page image was read, 'ocr' where only the machine-read text was used. Every quotation is from an image and was checked against it a second time before publication (see claude/tests/1675-light-claude.md). Not covered: Rohault on reflection, refraction and glasses (I.27 arts. XXXI-LII, pp. 305-321) beyond the machine-read text; Goudin on light and colour as sensible qualities (physics part 4, and t. 2); Le Grand's article on the sun and flame (V a. 13) and on vision; Sperling's chapter on qualities (II.3).
entry.built_with: Claude only (arm A of the Claude-vs-OpenRouter test, 2026-11-22)

quote_check.result: Every quotation re-read against its page image. Three transcriptions corrected before publication: Sperling p. 514 'omnesque' to the printed 'omnesq;'; Sperling p. 520 'alias' to the printed 'aliàs'; Goudin p. 98 'reflexa: Unde' to the printed 'reflexa :Vnde'. No change of sense; no misattributed or misplaced quotation. Sperling pp. 518-519: the word division of 'foris am-/bulantium' at the line end is not clear in the scan.

R.parts: Part I, ch. XXVII, 'De la Lumiere, & des Couleurs; du Transparent, & de l'Opaque', pp. 291-342 (vol. 1, MDZ canvas = page + 40)

S.parts: Book III, ch. V, 'De Luce', pp. 495-526 (MDZ canvas = page + 18; p. 518 misprinted 418)

G.parts: t. 3, physics part 2 (de mundo), q. II, a. IV, 'De affectionibus corporum caelestium, et praecipue de luce', pp. 95-104 (MDZ canvas = page + 20)

L.parts: Part V, a. XIV, 'De Lucis Natura', pp. 282-285; Part VIII, a. XVII, 'De Coloribus', pp. 511-513 (IA /page/n = page + 59 in Part V, + 60 in Part VIII)

placement.where: General physics (Part I), among the sensible qualities: after the chapter on sound and before the chapter on vision; light, colours, transparency and opacity in one chapter
Book III, after the chapters on the heavens and the stars (the book's contents from the machine-read table of contents)
Physics part 2, on the world: in the question on the heavens, as the chief property of the heavenly bodies
Light in Part V, on the world and the heavens, after the sun; colours in Part VIII, on man, as the object of sight before vision

claims.question: light-straight
claims.statement: The tendency of the subtle matter that makes secondary light is a tendency to go away in a straight line from the centre of the luminous body.

quote.orig: la tendance qu'a cette matiere à s'éloigner en ligne droite du centre du corps lumineux
quote.tr: the tendency that this matter has to go away in a straight line from the centre of the luminous body

rests_on.detail: the straight line is part of the definition of secondary light

claims.question: light-straight
claims.statement: The ray is a quality that leaps out from light straight and sharp; light in the medium (lumen) spreads sideways from light and the ray.

quote.orig: Radius est qualitas à luce exiliens in rectum & acutum.
quote.tr: The ray is a quality leaping out from light, straight and sharp.

claims.question: light-straight
claims.statement: The article read, on the light of the heavenly bodies, does not say how light travels.

claims.question: light-straight
claims.statement: Luminous bodies push the subtle matter away from themselves in every direction along straight lines.

rests_on.detail: the straight lines are part of the definition of light

claims.question: cold-light
claims.statement: Rotting wood, glow-worms and some flies shine in the dark; the stone of Bologna, found by an Italian chemist, after six hours in the fire and a while in the light, glows in the dark like a coal under ash.

claims.question: cold-light
claims.statement: A king of Scotland dressed men in shining fish scales with rotten wood for staves, and his nobles, taking them for spirits, fought and won.

claims.question: cold-light
claims.statement: The article read treats only the light of the heavenly bodies.

claims.question: cold-light
claims.statement: Many things give light without heat, as worms and rotten wood show; so light need not be joined with heat.

claims.question: light-nature
claims.statement: Primitive light is a certain motion of the parts of the luminous body, which pushes on every side the subtle matter in the pores of transparent bodies; secondary or derived light is that matter's tendency to move away in a straight line.

confidence.note: Received for now as a conjecture, which he expects to become 'une verité tres-certaine' once all the properties of light are deduced from it (p. 299).

reasons.detail: a pin causes pain by its figure and hardness, with nothing in it like the pain
the properties of light to be deduced from it

quote.orig: Ainsi, la lumiere primitive consistera dans un certain mouvement des parties du corps lumineux, qui les rend capables de pousser à la ronde la matiere subtile qui remplit les pores des corps transparent ; & l'inclination à se mouvoir, ou la tendance qu'a cette matiere à s'éloigner en ligne droite du centre du corps lumineux, constituëra l'essence de la lumiere seconde, ou dérivée.
quote.tr: Thus primitive light will consist in a certain motion of the parts of the luminous body, which makes them able to push on every side the subtle matter that fills the pores of transparent bodies; and the inclination to move, or the tendency that this matter has to go away in a straight line from the centre of the luminous body, will constitute the essence of secondary, or derived, light.

rests_on.detail: light a motion of the little balls of the second element (p. 322)

claims.question: light-nature
claims.statement: Aristotle, in the seventh chapter of the second book On the Soul, concludes that light is the act of the transparent as transparent, and that it is not fire nor a body passing from the luminous body.

quote.orig: la Lumiere est l'acte du transparent, entant que transparent
quote.tr: light is the act of the transparent, in so far as it is transparent

claims.question: light-nature
claims.statement: Light (lux) is the quality of a luminous body by which it is luminous and lights other things; the ray and the light spread through the medium (lumen) are qualities that come from it, and lumen is an accident, a spiritual or intentional being, nothing but an image of lux.

reasons.detail: Scaliger: light is a species, a representation of lux
lumen passes through glass, which no body could do

quote.orig: Lux est qualitas corporis lucidi, quâ ipsum lucidum est, & alia illuminat.
quote.tr: Light is the quality of a luminous body by which it is itself luminous and lights up other things.

claims.question: light-nature
claims.statement: Those who make lumen a body because it is reflected, wears the air and kindles fire, and because the first light was a body, are answered: sound, an accident, is reflected too, and the first light does not show that lumen is a substance.

reasons.detail: sound is reflected in the echo, and is an accident

claims.question: light-nature
claims.statement: The heavens have none of the elementary qualities; the sun heats because it has a higher quality, light, in which heat is eminently contained.

reasons.detail: incorruptible bodies cannot have qualities that tend to corruption and generation

quote.orig: Nec refert quod Sol calefaciat; ad id enim sufficit illum esse præditum qualitate quadam sublimiori, in qua eminenter contineatur calor, nempe luce.
quote.tr: Nor does it matter that the sun heats; for that it suffices that it be endowed with a certain higher quality in which heat is eminently contained, namely light.

rests_on.detail: the incorruptible heavens cannot have heat, so the sun heats by light

claims.question: light-nature
claims.statement: Light is nothing but a certain motion or action by which luminous bodies push the subtle matter away from themselves in every direction along straight lines; in the sun the matter of the first element strives to leave the centre and presses the globules of the second element around it.

reasons.detail: no one explains it better than the Author he follows

persons.name: René Descartes
persons.note: named in the title; on p. 283 'the Author whom I follow'

quote.orig: Dico, Lucem nihil aliud esse, quam motum quendam, vel actionem, qua corpora luminosa, materiam subtilem quaquaversum, secundum lineas rectas, à se propellunt.
quote.tr: I say that light is nothing other than a certain motion, or action, by which luminous bodies push subtle matter away from themselves in every direction along straight lines.

rests_on.detail: the first element in the sun presses the globules of the second

claims.question: light-nature
claims.statement: Those who say light is fire have weighty reasons but meet difficulties: two bodies would be in one place, many things give light without heat, so great a body could not perish in a moment when the sun sets, and the winds would block it.

reasons.detail: penetration of bodies; light without heat; where it goes at sunset; winds

rests_on.detail: many things give light without heat

rests_on.question: penetration
rests_on.detail: light as fire would put two bodies in one place

claims.question: light-act-transparent
claims.statement: He does not find Aristotle's doctrine fully satisfying: it leaves to be sought what the transparent body and the luminous body are, and what the presence of the second does in the first; on his own view the form of the transparent is the straightness of its pores.

quote.orig: je ne trouve pas qu'il y ait dequoy estre pleinement satisfait
quote.tr: I do not find that there is enough to be fully satisfied

claims.question: light-act-transparent
claims.statement: The transparent is transparent even without light, as fire is seen far off on a dark night; a man shut in a dark room sees the images of passers-by on the white wall; so light is in no way the act of the transparent. Rhodius is quoted to the same effect.

reasons.detail: the dark room: images through a chink
fire and stars seen through unlit air
Rhodius, Optics, book 1 ch. 8

quote.orig: Et notum est, hominem camera tenebrosa conclusum, per rimulam incidentes hominum foris ambulantium imagines in oppsito pariete albo videre posse depictas. Lumen ergò perspicui actum nullo modo esse censemus.
quote.tr: And it is well known that a man shut in a dark room can see the images of people walking outside, coming in through a small chink, painted on the white wall opposite. We therefore hold that light is in no way the act of the transparent.
quote.note: 'oppsito' as printed. Page 518 is misnumbered 418 in this copy.

claims.question: light-act-transparent
claims.statement: Not in the article read.

claims.question: light-act-transparent
claims.statement: Not in the articles read.

claims.question: light-time
claims.statement: Since secondary light is not an actual motion but a tendency, and the matter pushed is continuous, the luminous body, however far, acts in an instant, like a very long stick.

reasons.detail: a very long stick

quote.orig: il suit delà necessairement que le corps lumineux, pour éloigné qu'il soit, doit transmettre son action & se faire sentir en un instant ; à cause que cette matiere qu'il pousse est continuëment étenduë ; & que semblable en cela à un baston qui seroit fort long, le corps lumineux ne sçauroit pousser la plus proche, que celle qui est la plus éloignée ne se trouve en mesme-temps disposée à se mouvoir, & à avancer.
quote.tr: it follows necessarily that the luminous body, however far off it is, must transmit its action and make itself felt in an instant, because the matter it pushes is continuously extended; and that, like a very long stick in this, the luminous body cannot push the nearest part without the farthest being at the same time disposed to move and to advance.

rests_on.detail: secondary light is a tendency, not an actual motion

rests_on.question: void
rests_on.detail: the matter pushed is continuously extended, like a very long stick

claims.question: light-time
claims.statement: Against the common opinion that the motion of light is momentary: every motion has tendency, progress and succession; Toletus's arguments against motion in an instant conclude for light too; the nearer place is reached sooner; and twilight, with its lessened light, shows that light moves in time.

reasons.detail: every motion has progress and succession
Toletus, Physics book 4 ch. 8 q. 9
twilight

quote.orig: Certè terminum propiorem citiùs attingere lumen, quàm remotiorem, nullus unquam ibit inficias. In tempore ergò movetur, morasque patitur.
quote.tr: Certainly no one will ever deny that light reaches a nearer end sooner than a more distant one. It therefore moves in time, and suffers delay.

claims.question: light-time
claims.statement: He reports the opinion that light moves not in time but in a moment, because it meets no positive contrary and because of its supreme excellence, and rejects it.

quote.orig: Omnem motum in tempore fieri, communis aliàs assertio est. Et tamen luminis motum, non in tempore, non successivum sed momentaneum esse, censent.
quote.tr: That every motion takes place in time is otherwise a common assertion. And yet they hold that the motion of light is not in time, not successive, but momentary.

claims.question: light-time
claims.statement: Not in the article read.

claims.question: light-time
claims.statement: Light spreads to any distance in the least moment of time, since it consists not in the duration of a motion but in a sudden action or pressure, as a stick presses at both ends at once.

reasons.detail: a stick, by which at night we find water, stones and mud

quote.orig: Ita ut minimo temporis momento, Lux ad quamcunque distantiam diffundatur.
quote.tr: So that light is spread to any distance in the least moment of time.

rests_on.detail: light is a sudden action or pressure, not the duration of a motion

claims.question: colours
claims.statement: Since light is a motion of the little balls of the second element, colours are the modifications this motion can take from the surfaces of bodies: white from a rough surface that sends back the light it receives; black from a surface that sends back little; red, yellow and blue from balls that have less tendency to go straight and turn about their own centres.

reasons.detail: the prism
goldsmiths whiten silver by roughening it and take the whiteness off by polishing

rests_on.detail: since light is a motion of the balls of the second element, colours are its modifications

claims.question: colours
claims.statement: Light is not colour, as sense shows and reason declares: in darkness we see light but not colours; light illuminates and colour cannot; light makes a subject luminous, colour makes it coloured. Zabarella's view that light is a colour is rejected.

quote.orig: Lucem colorem non esse, monstrat Sensus, dictitat Ratio.
quote.tr: That light is not colour, sense shows and reason declares.

rests_on.detail: light is the quality that makes a body luminous; colour makes it coloured

claims.question: colours
claims.statement: The colours of earthly bodies are not in the article read; for the colours of the stars see colours-apparent.

claims.question: colours
claims.statement: Colours in general are nothing but the various ways bodies receive the rays and send them back to the eyes; rays reflected may take a circular motion, as a ball does; white and black suffice to compose all others.

reasons.detail: the colours of the rainbow, peacocks' tails and doves' necks

quote.orig: Dico, Colores in genere, nihil aliud sunt, quam varii modi, quibus corpora radios à corpore luminoso emissos, recipiunt, & ad oculos remittunt.
quote.tr: I say that colours in general are nothing other than the various ways in which bodies receive the rays sent out from a luminous body, and send them back to the eyes.

claims.question: colours-apparent
claims.statement: There is no foundation for dividing colours into true or real and false or apparent, nor into fixed and passing: the prism is as real as the tapestry and the same light makes us sense both; any falsity is in the judgment that follows vision.

reasons.detail: the same light acts in both cases

quote.orig: Mais je n'estime pas qu'il y ait aucun fondement en cette division, puis qu'il n'y a ny plus ny moins de realité aux unes qu'aux autres ; Car si le sentiment de couleur qu'on experimente en regardant une tapisserie est réel, celuy que l'on a en regardant au trauers d'un prisme ne l'est pas moins ; le prisme n'est pas moins réel que la tapisserie ; Et enfin, c'est la mesme lumiere qui intervient, pour nous faire sentir les couleurs du prisme, que pour nous faire sentir les autres.
quote.tr: But I do not think there is any foundation for this division, since there is neither more nor less reality in the one than in the others. For if the sensation of colour one has in looking at a tapestry is real, the one had in looking through a prism is no less so; the prism is no less real than the tapestry; and finally, it is the same light that comes in to make us sense the colours of the prism as to make us sense the others.

rests_on.detail: the same light makes the colours of the prism and of the tapestry

claims.question: colours-apparent
claims.statement: Lumen is not a real (material) being but a spiritual one, like the image in a mirror and all apparent colours.

quote.orig: Atque sic lumen ens reale non est, sed spiritale. Non secus ac imago in speculo, omnesq; colores apparentes.
quote.tr: And in this sense light is not a real being but a spiritual one, just like the image in a mirror and all apparent colours.

claims.question: colours-apparent
claims.statement: The heavens are tinged with no colour, being perfectly transparent; what appears as colour in the heavenly bodies is not true colour but a modification of the light they give out or reflect.

quote.orig: Sideribus verò pro colore lux inesse videtur, vel propria vel reflexa :Vnde hæc diversitas colori non est nisi diversa modificatio lucis
quote.tr: In the stars light seems to be present in place of colour, either their own or reflected; so this diversity of colour is nothing but a different modification of light
quote.note: 'Vnde' and the spacing of the colon as printed.

rests_on.detail: the incorruptible, perfectly transparent heavens can have no true colour

claims.question: colours-apparent
claims.statement: All colours are true and none merely apparent: the nature of colour consists only in appearing and being seen, and it is a contradiction that something should appear and be false.

reasons.detail: to appear and be false is a contradiction

quote.orig: Repugnat enim, ut aliquid appareat, & falsum sit
quote.tr: For it is a contradiction that something should appear and be false

claims.question: explanation-standard
claims.statement: Light in bodies need be nothing like our sensation, as a pin's figure and hardness are nothing like pain; what is offered is a conjecture about matter and motion, to be confirmed by deducing all the properties of light from it.

reasons.detail: the pin and pain

quote.orig: Je ne pretens pas maintenant que tout cela soit autrement receu que comme une simple conjecture
quote.tr: I do not claim for now that all this should be received otherwise than as a simple conjecture

claims.question: explanation-standard
claims.statement: The questions are put in the categories of the schools: whether light is substance or accident, quality, real or intentional; answers are drawn from the senses, from reason and from authorities, Aristotle, Zabarella, Scaliger and Toletus among them.

claims.question: explanation-standard
claims.statement: No one, so far as he knows, explains the nature of light better than the Author he follows; placing the force of light in a pressure of the subtle matter frees him from the penetration of bodies and from joining light to heat.

quote.orig: A nullo quod sciam, melius quam ab Authore quem sequor, Lucis Natura explicatur.
quote.tr: By no one, so far as I know, is the nature of light better explained than by the Author whom I follow.

claims.question: heavens-matter
claims.statement: The phenomena of the moon confirm that the lunar body is incorruptible and different from the elements here; the heavens may not have elementary qualities, which tend to corruption and generation.

claims.question: scripture-nature
claims.statement: Where light comes from the Spirit of the Lord revealed: God said, let there be light; God's question to Job is not meant to forbid the inquiry but to show the abyss of his wisdom.

claims.question: first-day-light
claims.statement: The light made on the first day was neither an accident nor a spirit but a body, placed about the abyss of the waters as the stars are about the air, which by its motion made the first three days; those who make it a quality are answered.

reasons.detail: Genesis 1:3
the term of creation is a substance

claims.question: first-day-light
claims.statement: Not in the chapter read.

claims.question: first-day-light
claims.statement: Not in the article read.

claims.question: first-day-light
claims.statement: Not in the articles read.

claims.question: star-light
claims.statement: Not only the sun but the fixed stars shine by their own light: so distant from the sun they could borrow little or none, and yet they are most radiant.

reasons.detail: the stars' brightness at their distance

quote.orig: Non modò Sol sed etiam Stellæ fixæ fulgent propriâ luce.
quote.tr: Not only the sun but also the fixed stars shine with their own light.

claims.question: star-light
claims.statement: All the planets borrow from the sun the light that strikes our eyes, as their phases and shadows show; yet all, the moon included, seem to have some light of their own, too faint to reach us.

reasons.detail: the moon; the phases of Venus in the telescope; Mars; Jupiter's satellites in its shadow; the shadow of Saturn's ring
light is the property most akin to the heavenly bodies

rests_on.detail: light the property most akin to the heavenly bodies

claims.question: moon-ashen-light
claims.statement: The faint secondary light seen on the crescent moon is not its own, for it vanishes at the quadratures and in a central eclipse; the commoner and truer opinion is that it comes from the earth, against Tycho, who made it come from Venus. A sunlit spot on a wall lights a room forty feet across, so the sunlit half of the earth can light the moon.

reasons.detail: it vanishes at the quadratures and in a central eclipse
a sunlit spot lights a dark hall

quote.orig: Lux illa secundaria, quæ apparet in Luna crescente ante priorem quadraturam; item in ea decrescente post alteram quadraturam; & demum in ea eclipsim patiente non videtur illi propria.
quote.tr: That secondary light which appears in the moon when waxing before the first quarter, and likewise when waning after the second quarter, and finally when it suffers an eclipse, does not seem to be its own.

claims.question: sky-blue
claims.statement: The blue of the sky is not in the heavens, which are perfectly transparent, but is caused by the excessive depth of the transparent, in which the light, above all the sun's, is absorbed and degenerates into that colour; for the same cause the sea and the air round distant mountains look blue.

quote.orig: Cæruleus ergo ille color insitus illis non est, sed causatus ex nimia diaphani profunditate in qua lux præcipuè Solaris, quæ nunquam cœlis occidit, absorpta degenerat in ejusmodi colorem
quote.tr: That blue colour is therefore not inherent in them, but caused by the excessive depth of the transparent, in which light, above all the sun's, which never sets in the heavens, is absorbed and degenerates into a colour of this kind
quote.note: The scan's 'Cæruleus' has a damaged initial; the 'C' is not legible.

rests_on.detail: the blue of the sky is light modified in the deep transparent, not a colour of the heavens

claims.question: sky-blue
claims.statement: Blue, nearest to black, belongs to what reflects few rays; deep, clear sea water looks blue because few rays are sent back from its surface and none of those that enter it return.

rests_on.detail: blue, nearest black, belongs to what sends back few rays

claims.question: fire-light-same
claims.statement: Light cannot be fire (margin heading): many things shine without heat, and two bodies would be in one place.

rests_on.detail: many things shine without heat

rests_on.question: penetration
rests_on.detail: light as fire would put two bodies in one place

claims.question: fire-light-same
claims.statement: The sun heats not by heat, which the heavens lack, but by light, a higher quality in which heat is eminently contained.

rests_on.detail: the heavens lack heat, an elementary quality
the sun heats by light, a higher quality containing heat eminently
